articles.standfirst: El base nacionalizado español jugó 26 partidos con los Raptors en la temporada de su campeonato, pero fue cortado y la franquicia nunca le reconoció con la preciada pieza
articles.summary: El base nacionalizado español jugó 26 partidos con los Raptors en la temporada de su campeonato, pero fue cortado y la franquicia nunca le reconoció con la preciada pieza
articles.body: Lorenzo Brown todavía sigue esperando un anillo de campeón que difícilmente le va a llegar. El base nacionalizado español jugó en los Raptors que se llevaron el título en la temporada 2018-19, pero fue cortado y, pese a haber ayudado al equipo, nunca le dieron la pieza que le acreditaría como ganador de la NBA. En estas ocasiones, la decisión de dar ese anillo es de la franquicia, aunque se acostumbra a hacer una copia para todos los jugadores que han colaborado en el éxito. En el caso de Lorenzo el de Albacete, como le rebautizaron en su paso por la selección española, no se lo entregaron. El jugador de 36 años, que actualmente pertenece al Armani Milán pero está cedido en el Hapoel Jerusalén, disputó aquella campaña 26 de los 42 primeros encuentros de la franquicia de Toronto. Su papel fue limitado con medias de 8,2 minutos, 2,1 puntos y 1,1 asistencias. "Me despidieron en enero de ese año. Estuve allí. Estuve allí trabajando, hombre", se lamentó Brown en el podcast 'Run Your Race'. Su último partido con los Raptors fue el 6 de enero y al día siguiente fue cortado para no volver a jugar nunca más en la NBA. El internacional español no fue el único jugador que militó en el equipo canadiense aquella temporada y se quedó sin anillo. Jonas Valanciunas, CJ Miles y Delon Wright fueron enviados a Memphis en el traspaso de Marc Gasol e, incluso teniendo más protagonismo que Brown, tampoco recibieron la preciada pieza.

articles.title: Las Dream pasan por encima de las Valkyries y fuerzan el séptimo partido
articles.standfirst: El decisivo choque se disputa en San Francisco del sábado al domingo (01.00)
articles.summary: El decisivo choque se disputa en San Francisco del sábado al domingo (01.00)
articles.body: Las Atlanta Dream mantienen su sueño (dream) de ser campeonas de la WNBA en su cuarta final. Se enfrentaban a su primer match ball que solventaron, ganando el sexto partido en Atlanta, 80-69 y forzando el séptimo partido. Dicho de otra forma, las Golden State Valkyries perdieron su primera oportunidad de ganar el anillo en tan sólo su segundo año de vida. La derrota fue contundente, pero tendrán otra ocasión en la madrugada del sábado al domingo en San Francisco en el partido decisivo. Será el decimotercer partido decisivo en la historia, el primero Game 7 desde que en 2025 la WNBA adoptó el formato al mejor de siete partidos en las Finales. El sexto partido en Atlanta, jugado a una hora poco habitual en EEUU, se decidió muy rápido. El primer cuarto fue un recital de las locasles, 32-15 y al descanso el partido estaba casi decidido, 46-21. Las de San Francisco trataron de reaccionar en el un tercer cuarto que ganaron, 17-21, pero las Dream acabaron llevándose el triunfo. Con Gaby Williams despertando en el segundo tiempo, las Valkyries se acercaron al final gracias a su aportación (74-61), pero el día de las jugadoras de Atlanta que bajaron el ritmo al final sin perder el control del partido. El empeño de Williams llevó a las Valkyries a su menos desventaja en más de 30 minutos de partido, 77-69 a 1:09, pero un triple de Gray cerró cualquier tipo de sorpresa al final. En las Dream, que jugaron con siete jugadoras entre la lesionadas y las que no pisaron la cancha, destacaron Alisha Gray, con 23 puntos y 4/5 en triples, Rhyne Howard, 21 y Angel Reese, 15 puntos y 14 rebotes aunque 2/8 en triples. A lo largo de la temporada siempre que Reese ha anotado tres o más triples, las Dream ganaron. En las Valkyries, Gaby Williams fue la mejor con 26 puntos, Pero su primer tiempo pasó factura. Hizo 1/8 en tiros de campo y estuvo muy fallona incluso en la distribución con tres pérdidas. En la segunda parte mejoró hasta el 6/10 en tiro. Además, Tiffany Hayes aportó 15 puntos. En la madrugada de domingo al lunes (01.00), habrá un nuevo campeón de la NBA para suceder a Las Vegas Aces.

articles.title: Angel Reese Makes History as Dream Beat Valkyries in WNBA Finals G6, Box Score Stats & Highlights
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream had no designs on ending their season on a Thursday afternoon.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream had no designs on ending their season on a Thursday afternoon.

The 2026 WNBA Finals is heading to a winner-take-all Game 7 after the Dream held off the Golden State Valkyries 80-69.

Atlanta stars Angel Reese, Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard all filled out the stat sheet. It was a different story for Golden State as it didn't have the defensive effort to compensate for Veronica Burton putting in a poor game and Gabby Williams being sluggish to start.

Reese is up to 78 rebounds in the series, which is the most ever in a single WNBA Finals.

The Dream stormed out of the gates in a way nobody expected.

In Game 5, Atlanta didn't have 32 points until the 4:05 mark of the third quarter. On Thursday, that's how many Karl Smesko's squad had after just one quarter of action.

The Dream's offense cooled off from there, but they built a big enough buffer to where this wasn't much of a contest. Their lead swelled to as many as 25 points before Golden State started chipping away at the deficit in the third quarter.

The Valkyries got the gap down to 13 points with a little under seven minutes remaining in the game, but a pair of long-range jumpers from Gray and Reese brought their momentum to a halt.

Three-point shooting was a big differentiator for the two teams. The Dream were 13-of-30 from beyond the arc compared to 7-of-27 for the Valkyries.

The series will shift to Ballhalla for Game 7 on Saturday. Chase Center has become one of the most intimidating road atmospheres in the WNBA, but the Dream won't be overawed after claiming Game 2 on the road.

On one hand, the Valkyries should be encouraged by the fact they can't play much worse in the Finals decider. There's going to be some positive regression.

On the other hand, it's perhaps more worrying that Golden State has scored fewer than 70 points in all but one of the first six games. They're putting a lot of pressure on their defense, which means it only takes one bad quarter to put them in serious trouble.

Inside the other locker room, Atlanta's performance after the first quarter will be a concern. The Dream and Valkyries were evenly matched after the opening 10 minutes. Golden State

Especially on the road, Atlanta can't afford to take its foot off the gas like it did in Game 6 if it gains the advantage early on.

articles.title: WNBA: Atlanta Dream set up Finals decider against Golden State Valkyries
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream deny the Golden State Valkyries their first WNBA Finals victory after an 80-69 win forces the series into a seventh and deciding game on Sunday.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream denied the Golden State Valkyries their first WNBA Finals victory after an 80-69 win forced the series into a seventh and deciding game on Sunday.

The Valkyries, who led 3-2 heading into the game in Atlanta, got off to a slow start, trailing 32-15 at the end of the first quarter.

That proved pivotal as the hosts maintained a healthy buffer throughout the game, leading 46-26 at half-time.

Despite not being at her best, Golden State Valkyries star Gabby Williams was the game's top scorer with 26 points, while Angel Reese led the rebounding charts with 14.

Kiah Stokes kept Reese, who is in her first season with the Dream after being traded from the Chicago Sky, quiet in Game Five, but was unable to replicate that performance.

The 24-year-old delivered another standout performance after her Game Two display made her the youngest player, and only the third overall, to record at least 30 points and 15 rebounds in a Finals series.

It was a superb performance from Karl Smesko's side, who had no room for error as they kept what has been a thrilling series alive.

Game Six of the series was originally scheduled for 20:00 local time at Gateway Center Arena, which has a capacity of 3,500, but was moved to State Farm Arena and brought forward to 12:30 local time amid concerns over a scheduling clash with the Atlanta Hawks.

"Our concerns did not receive the attention nor the urgency that they deserved. We earned our place in the Finals, and our city deserves the opportunity to show up for its team," the Dream said in an open letter.

State Farm Arena, which has a capacity of 16,888, was sold out for the game.

Having suffered back-to-back defeats, the hosts will rue the missed opportunity to clinch the title in front of a large home crowd.

However, they will head into Sunday's deciding game at Chase Center in San Francisco (00:00 BST) full of confidence.

articles.title: Angel Reese Reacts to Historic Performance in Dream's WNBA Finals Game 6 Win over Valkyries
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese commented following her team's series-extending, 80-69 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese commented following her team's series-extending, 80-69 win over the Golden State Valkyries in Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Thursday.

Reese addressed the victory in a post on X after dropping 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists in 35 minutes of action:

The third-year forward made history during Game 6, as she broke Sylvia Fowles' record for the most total rebounds ever accrued during a WNBA Finals series:

Speaking during an on-court interview after Thursday's win, Reese discussed the upcoming Game 7 on Saturday, saying, "Championship mentality. We just wanted to get this one, one at a time, and being able to go out and take our chances on going on the road and win one. We needed the opportunity, that's all we needed, and we maximized it today. I'm just really proud of this group, the job is not done, and I'm looking forward to it. One more."

The Dream's backs were against the wall entering Thursday's home game, as the Valkyries were one win away from winning their first WNBA championship in only their second year of existence.

Atlanta dominated from start to finish in Game 6, though, racing out to a 32-15 lead in the first quarter that was never relinquished.

Reese felt the fast start was the key to Thursday's win, telling reporters , "I'm proud of this group for the punch first that we emphasized. When we punch first, we have won every single game. ... We have to make sure we continue that going forward."

Fittingly, the highly competitive series is shifting back to San Francisco for Game 7, which will be played at the Chase Center on Halloween night.

The Dream won Game 2 in San Francisco, so they know what it takes to beat a tough Valkyries team on the road.

Atlanta used a balanced attack to beat Golden State in Game 6 with four players scoring in double figures, and should that happen again in Game 7, the Dream stand a great chance of winning their first-ever WNBA title.

articles.title: WNBA bailed out of scheduling disaster as Angel Reese, Dream force Game 7
articles.summary: Angel Reese struggled shooting again but the Atlanta Dream forced a WNBA Finals Game 7 as Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard caught fire from three.
articles.body: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream kept their championship hopes alive Thursday. Perhaps more importantly, they spared the WNBA a title celebration in the middle of a workday. The Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 80-69 at State Farm Arena, evening the best-of-seven Finals at 3-3 and forcing a deciding game Saturday at 8 p.m. ET at Chase Center in San Francisco. Reese struggled to shoot the ball for a third consecutive game, finishing with 15 points on 5-for-18 shooting. She grabbed 14 rebounds and dished out six assists but also committed six turnovers. THE WNBA'S DRAMA-FILLED SEASON COMES TO A CRASHING END That made it three straight games with more turnovers than made field goals for the Dream star. Across Games 4, 5 and 6, Reese shot 9-for-38 from the floor (24%) and turned the ball over 15 times. This time, Atlanta had enough offense around her. Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard added 21, combining to make nine of their 13 three-point attempts. Their shooting also ensured that the WNBA’s championship would be decided in prime time. The league moved Game 6 from its originally scheduled 8 p.m. start to 12:30 p.m. Thursday to accommodate an arena doubleheader with the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks, who were hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers that night. Golden State fans back home had to tune in at 9:30 a.m. to watch their team try to win its first title. There had also been questions about where the Valkyries would celebrate if they won. ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne reported that a championship celebration could be moved to a practice court to accommodate preparations for the Hawks game. She later clarified that there was "a resolve" to make sure any championship won Thursday was celebrated on the court. But that sounded an awful lot like damage control from the WNBA. Winning a championship and then moving the celebration to a practice court because the NBA needed the floor would have been a terrible look for the league. Atlanta’s win made the issue moot. The crowd deserved credit for showing up under the circumstances. State Farm Arena was largely filled for a Thursday afternoon, although there were more empty seats and the building was quieter at the start than it had been for Games 3 and 4. Fans who spoke with OutKick outside the arena described taking time off work, pulling children out of school and difficult travel times to attend. Tiffany Hayes’ father, Renard Hayes, blamed the league and Atlanta for the scheduling predicament. DREAM, VALKYRIES LEAVE COURT BEFORE TI’S 10-YEAR-OLD DAUGHTER SINGS WNBA FINALS ANTHEM Before tipoff, both teams again left the court for the national anthem, this time performed by rapper T.I.’s 10-year-old daughter, Heiress Harris. It was their sixth consecutive absence during the Finals. Once the game began, Atlanta quickly took control. The Dream made six of their eight first-quarter three-point attempts and built a 32-15 lead. Reese made only one of her four shots in the period, but contributed four assists, including passes that set up three of Atlanta’s threes. Atlanta pushed its advantage to 25 points in the second quarter and took a 46-26 lead into halftime. Golden State narrowed the deficit in the third, but Atlanta still led 63-47 entering the fourth. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Reese scored five points in the final period, making a driving layup and a three-pointer with Atlanta already leading by double digits. She finished 2-for-8 from beyond the arc. The Valkyries eventually got within eight. Gabby Williams completed a three-point play with 1:15 remaining, cutting Atlanta’s lead to 77-69 and fouling Howard out of the game. Gray answered on the next possession, making a three-pointer off a Reese assist with 56 seconds left. That restored Atlanta’s double-digit lead and provided the final points of the afternoon. Gray finished 8-for-12 from the field and 5-for-7 from three. Howard made four of her six three-point attempts, while Atlanta went 13-for-30 as a team. Williams led Golden State with 26 points but shot 8-for-22. The Valkyries made just 22 of their 70 field-goal attempts. Kiah Stokes, whose defense had been a major factor throughout the series, went scoreless and failed to block a shot in 20 minutes. That ended her streak of six consecutive playoff games with at least three blocks. Reese and the Dream head to San Francisco for Game 7, with both franchises one win from their first championship. articles.title: Raptors' Kawhi Leonard expected to miss more time than first expected with knee injury
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors went all in for Kawhi Leonard this summer. Leonard has suffered a knee injury that seems to be more severe than originally thought.
articles.body:
This summer was a big one for the Toronto Raptors as they look to get back into championship conversations. Toronto knew heading into the offseason that they were going to do whatever it takes to build a roster that could legitimately compete.

In doing so, they found themselves with an opportunity to bring back a very familiar face in Kawhi Leonard. The trade for Leonard was made official in the middle of September.

"The trade sending Kawhi Leonard from the LA Clippers to Toronto has been made official after a monthslong delay due to the NBA's investigation into the Clippers for salary cap circumvention. The teams initially agreed to the deal on June 30, but it was paused while the league investigated allegations the Clippers violated salary cap rules in signing Leonard as a free agent," ESPN's Shams Charania wrote.

However, on Tuesday, Leonard went down with a knee injury that was initially expected to sideline him for only about a week.

"Kawhi Leonard will be sidelined for at least a week because of swelling in his left knee, the Toronto Raptors said Tuesday. Leonard, who has a long history of knee problems, was a late scratch from Toronto's game against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Sunday. The Raptors said tests revealed there is no acute injury in his left knee," NBA.com wrote.

This is a big blow for the Raptors, as Leonard was starting to find his footing and build chemistry with his new team. NBA reporter Chris Haynes reported Thursday that Leonard's injury is worse than originally thought.

"Toronto Raptors star Kawhi Leonard (knee) is expected to be sidelined for at least 3-4 weeks, sources tell me," Haynes posted.

That is another devastating blow for Toronto, as the team may have to go almost a full month without its superstar. The two-time NBA champion will focus on getting healthy before returning to the court.

Leonard returned to Toronto because that is where his family wanted to be. He also wants to win another championship, so when he returns, he will be eager to help make that happen.

articles.title: NBA ratings still rising to start new season
articles.summary: The NBA saw encouraging ratings growth in the first year of its new broadcast deals with ESPN, NBC, and Amazon Prime Video thanks to additional broadcast exp...
articles.body:
The NBA saw encouraging ratings growth in the first year of its new broadcast deals with ESPN, NBC, and Amazon Prime Video thanks to additional broadcast exposure and a burgeoning crop of young stars.

That success is now continuing in the second year of those media deals.

According to Sports Business Journal's Austin Karp , the league is seeing a 19% increase in primetime windows across its television partners to start the new campaign. The NBA is averaging 3.33 million viewers in its first eight primetime matchups.

Regular-season viewership soared 16% in the first year of the new media deals as the NBA began a new television era across broadcast, cable, and streaming. Playoff viewership was also strong, with the NBA Finals posting its best ratings since the Chicago Bulls' 1998 championship.

Heading into year two, the NBA is doubling down on what brought it success last season. The league is expanding its broadcast network windows even further, from 75 games last season to 90 this season. Only 19 games aired on network TV in the final year of the former media deals. Additionally, the league is leaning into featuring more teams in hopes that more stars become household names. This year a record 24 teams will make at least five national television appearances.

Each network is seeing growth in the early part of its broadcast schedule. NBC had the most-watched tipoff game ever with Knicks-Sixers reaching 7.7 million viewers. ESPN celebrated its best opening week since 2014, with an average of 2.3 million viewers. Most importantly, Amazon more than doubled viewership for its season-opening doubleheader, with 2.14 million fans tuning in.

It will still take time for basketball fans to get used to the broadcasting rhythm of which games are on which networks on certain nights. But these numbers show that fans might be becoming more acclimated to the new setup, and the increased exposure is helping the league on all fronts.

articles.title: Minus Luka Doncic, Lakers Bounce Back Against Clippers Behind New Additions Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers' first loss of the season (a 136-129 defeat at home Wednesday night against Portland) meant the team had to bounce back. Unfortunately...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers' first loss of the season (a 136-129 defeat at home Wednesday night against Portland) meant the team had to bounce back. Unfortunately, they found themselves playing shorthanded without their unquestioned leader and another starter just 24 hours later against the crosstown rival Los Angeles Clippers.

Completing a back-to-back in the midst of five games in seven days, the Lakers were without superstar Luka Doncic due to back tightness. Meanwhile, fellow starter Ziaire Williams was sidelined due to left foot soreness. Still, behind the end-to-end play of new additions Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton , the Lakers (4-1) collectively filled the 50-point void of Doncic's absence and were able to get back on track following a 103-87 win.

"It's just a testament to all the guys," Grimes said after the game . "I mean, everybody coming in with the right mindset, coming in not worrying about trying to fill the void that Luka [left] and trying to make up 35, 40 points. Everybody came in and did it collectively, and I feel like it's just a testament to the team and just how we want to play for each other and get the win."

Sliding into the starting lineup in place of Doncic, Grimes led the way to the win by scoring 23 points on 7-of-15 shooting. He also recorded three rebounds, five assists, and four steals, giving the Lakers a spark at both ends of the floor. All told, the Lakers ended the night with six scorers in double figures, including Sexton's 21 points on 6-of-11 shooting and 4-for-7 from three-point range in 21 minutes off the bench. And according to Grimes, it was Sexton's energy in a reserve role that led to his own success.

"It's contagious. Everybody wants to play that hard when you see somebody else giving maximum effort like that." Grimes said of Sexton.

"I think just bringing that juice," Sexton added . "I come into the game and try to impact on the defensive end. I know what I can do offensively, but I just want to come in and be a pest and be someone who changes the game on the defensive side."

Grimes joined the Lakers on a four-year deal reportedly worth $60 million this offseason after stints with New York, Detroit, Dallas and Philadelphia during his first five seasons in the NBA. For his career, Grimes has averaged 11.1 points, 3.2 rebounds and 2.3 assists in 323 games. He has connected on 44.6 percent from the field and 36.5 percent from three-point range, making him a valuable contributor to the Lakers' roster. He's also shown the ability to slide into the starting lineup when needed, making 147 starts in his career. That was certainly needed Wednesday night with Doncic out of the lineup.

Likewise, Sexton joined the Lakers on a reported two-year deal worth $19.2 million after spending time with Cleveland, Utah, Chicago and Charlotte. For his career, Sexton holds averages of 18.3 points, 2.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists, connecting on 47.2 percent from the field and 38.8 percent from three-point range in 479 games. However, it was the defensive intensity Grimes and Sexton provided Wednesday night that Lakers Head Coach JJ Redick credits for the win.

The Lakers' defense held the Clippers to 35.1 percent shooting from the field and 32.3 percent from behind the three-point arc, forcing 24 turnovers and collecting 15 steals as a team. It was a glimpse of how potent the Lakers' defense has a chance of becoming this season, according to Redick. And if the Lakers' defense can match their explosive offense, the team could find itself in championship contention.

"Q [Grimes] got a couple of steals (in the first half), and Collin was into the basketball," Redick detailed . "[Sexton] literally switched onto the basketball three straight times, and then Q gets a steal and goes down and lays it in. That stretch, that play was very emblematic of how our defense was tonight."

Redick added: "We've seen some of the stuff defensively for our group where we're like, 'All right, we can be good.' We have a lot of things we got to get better at, but we have kind of the makeup to be a decent defensive team, if not a really good defensive team."

The Lakers will try to build on the momentum of Wednesday's win when they return to action Friday night against Golden State. The Lakers will also begin group play of the Emirates NBA Cup, which has both the Lakers and Warriors featured in West Group C. Things don't get any easier after that when the Lakers welcome the Toronto Raptors on Sunday.

articles.summary: The New York Knicks' financial future has generated plenty of headlines in the early portion of the 2026-27 NBA season, and they are reportedly making a move with an eye on creating more salary cap space down the line.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks' financial future has generated plenty of headlines in the early portion of the 2026-27 NBA season, and they are reportedly making a move with an eye on creating more salary cap space down the line.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday the Knicks are planning to decline the fourth-year option on Pacôme Dadiet's deal.

The option is worth $5.37 million, so the Knicks will have more salary space without it. What's more, Charania noted the two sides "could still discuss a reunion" since the move will make the forward an unrestricted free agent during the upcoming offseason.

Blockbuster Trade to Fix Miami's Bam Problem 💡

Of more note is what this means for some of the headline players.

New York released a statement earlier this month revealing it was pausing contract negotiations.

Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart are among those who are eligible for an extension. Towns even said he was "very disappointed, to say the least" when the Knicks released that statement, per The Athletic's James L. Edwards III .

For his part, Hart said , "Everything is going to work out. I'm not really too stressed over it. I'm not putting too much into it. We have expectations, so it's good we are able to focus on the season."

Even the smallest increase in salary cap space is notable for the Knicks given the uncertain futures of so many players, so it comes as no surprise the team is reportedly declining Dadiet's option.

After all, he is not much of a contributor who has appeared in just one minute of action this season after averaging 4.7 minutes a night in 29 games last season.

While he was a first-round pick in 2024, he is yet to establish himself as an important part of the Knicks' rotation and could be looking for a new team next offseason.

articles.summary: El ala-pívot finlandés pidió el cambio inmediatamente y se retiró en el segundo cuarto para no volver a salir del vestuario
articles.body: En mitad de otra gran noche del Real Madrid, la que le dio la décima victoria consecutiva, una mala noticia. Mikael Jantunen se lesionó en el segundo cuarto y parece grave. El jugador finlandés se lastimó sin sufrir torcedura ni golpe. Acudía al rebote de ataque en una jugada y segundos después ya estaba pidiendo el cambio. Había notado algo. Jantunen se fue cojeando al banquillo y allí fue explorado por miembros del servicio médico del equipo blanco. Después se levantó y, también cojeando, se marchó a los vestuarios para no volver a salir. "Es un problema en la fascia y no tiene buena pinta. Mañana le harán pruebas y veremos. No sabemos el alcance de la lesión, pero no creo que juegue esta semana ni la siguiente", dijo Pedro Martínez sobre la lesión de su jugador. Martínez aseguró que "la lesión es muy similar a la de Nick Smith Jr., pero no es lo mismo si es una rotura parcial o completa. También depende de cada jugador. Nick no se rompió, lo cual es una buena noticia, porque no creemos que sea de larga duración. Con Jantunen hay que esperar para ver el alcance".
